the use of fluorescent Ca2+-sensors in studies of Ca2+ homeostasis in living cells and tissues.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mitochondria are capable of converting the acetoxymethylester forms of these indicators into Ca2+-sensing forms, but that the mitochondrial contribution to intracellular fura-2 Ca2+ measurements is likely to be small.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the mitochondrial conversion of esterified forms of fura 2 and indo 1 to Ca2+ -sensitive forms is a potential problem in the measurement of intracellular free Ca2+ by these indicators, and that the problem can be avoided by the use of mitochondria inhibitors or by the use of the esters of fura-4F and indo-4F.
